title: "Tags"

# Tags: Lightweight vs Annotated

After this page you can mark a commit as a release and push that name.

## Two kinds

```bash
cd ~/desk/desk-api
git tag v0.1.0                    # lightweight: a ref file
git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "desk-api 0.1.0"   # annotated: a tag object
```

**Lightweight** is a name pointing at a commit (like a branch that you do not move).

**Annotated** is a real object: message, tagger, date, optional signature (chapter 20). Releases should be annotated.

```text
 lightweight                         annotated

 refs/tags/v0.1.0 ──► commit C       refs/tags/v0.1.0 ──► tag object
                                                              │
                                                              ▼
                                                         commit C
                                         tag object has message, tagger, date
```

If `v0.1.0` already exists, Git refuses. `git tag -f` overwrites locally; moving a published tag surprises clones. Prefer `v0.1.1`.

## List and show

```bash
git tag
git tag -l 'v0.1.*'
git show v0.1.0
```

## Push

Tags are not pushed by default.

```bash
git push origin v0.1.0
git push origin --tags
```

`--tags` pushes all local tags. Prefer naming one tag for a release.

## Checkout

```bash
git switch --detach v0.1.0
```

Detached HEAD (chapter 1). Build or inspect, then `git switch main`. To develop from a tag: `git switch -c hotfix/0.1.1 v0.1.0`.

## Delete

```bash
git tag -d v0.1.0
git push origin --delete v0.1.0
```

Forges may still show a release page; that is forge metadata, not the Git tag.
